content:
An ideal agent is optimal relative to a specified problem
An optimality claim needs a model, utilities, available actions and information. It does not guarantee a favorable outcome in a hostile world or identify the right real-world model. Conflating formal optimality with success makes practical approximations look defective for failures no feasible policy could avoid.

quote: out of the valley and higher than
content:
Nonmonotonic progress is possible; the far peak is unproven
Interacting changes can make a partial implementation worse before a complete one becomes better. That logical possibility is real. It does not demonstrate that a specific struggling curriculum sits in such a valley; predeclared milestones, time limits and outside comparisons are needed to distinguish temporary costs from an ineffective method.

quote: signed up for cryonics, a sudden
content:
A contested application cannot define rationality by agreement
Cryonics involves empirical uncertainties and value judgments not settled by identifying familiar biases. Treating uptake as a diagnostic of rationality assumes the conclusion of that practical argument. A valid test should assess the quality of reasoning and calibration without awarding correctness merely for agreement with the author.
